s21d1_060_residuals.summary: 26 residual queries out of 80. 19 are shortlist-ceiling misses no reranker can reach, 7 are rerank-ordering misses.
named_structural_error_classes: rerank_ordering: a relevant pair was on the shortlist and the graph score failed to lift it into the top five. 7 queries, ids in the residual report.
score degeneracy: 2 distinct graph scores per query and 6 across the whole corpus; 61 of 80 rankings are decided by the pair-id tiebreak rather than by the arm.
s21d1_060_residuals.ties: 61 of 80 queries had the rank of their relevant pair decided inside a tied score block. For the 20 fresh logic and mathematics queries every completed comparison returned the identical 0.525424.
s21d1_060_residuals.regressions: 3, all of them the tie effect: the relevant pair sits in the arm's highest score block and still lands seventh. Two of the three had been ranked first by the vector arm.
s21d1_060_residuals.timeouts: 60 cutoff events over 20 queries, 3 per query, every one of them on a fresh logic or mathematics query. p50 24.69 ms, max 1789.09 ms against a declared 2 s budget.
s21d1_060_residuals.domain_concentration: coding holds 23 of the 26 residuals, 88.5%. Mathematics has none, logic has 3. All 26 are tier-1 queries.

projected_maximum_gain.method: oracle ordering of the current 10-candidate shortlist, which bounds every reranker

s21d1_060_residuals.binding_constraint: shortlist width, not the comparator. The reranker ceiling is 0.7625 at width 10, 0.9000 at 15, 0.9750 at 20 and 1.0000 at 30, and no query lacks a relevant pair in the pool.
s21d1_060_residuals.no_holdout_was_inspected: the report replays the frozen D1 benchmark only; no D2 holdout exists yet and none was read
s21d1_060_residuals.raw_result_linkage: every class lists its query ids, and the report carries all 80 per-query records with their returned pair ids and scores

s21d1_062_decision.scope: no FGW in D1, and no D2 experiment approved yet
s21d1_062_decision.projected_threshold: any reranker over the current shortlist is bounded at 0.7625 top-5 recall, which is +0.0875 over the arm already in place
s21d1_062_decision.latency_and_memory_budget: the existing arm already spends 60 cutoff events and 1788.9 ms at p95 within a 2 s budget, with 827.2 MB peak, on 80 pairs. A heavier comparator is not shown to fit.

section_4_11_conditions.projected_improvement_at_least_0_05: met on the ceiling: +0.2250 recall and +0.3233 MRR over the strongest simpler arm

s21d1_062_decision.why_not_a_go: 19 of 26 residual queries sit behind a shortlist a reranker never touches, the budget condition already fails for the cheaper comparator, and the lever that does reach those 19 changes one declared bound and adds nothing.
s21d1_062_decision.d2_disposition: widen vector_shortlist and re-measure first. Width 20 raises the reranker ceiling from 0.7625 to 0.9750, the only measured change that could carry the arm past the 0.70 recall and 0.50 MRR usefulness floor. The FGW question reopens only on a residual report taken after that lever which still shows rerank_ordering as the dominant residual.
s21d1_062_decision.no_unused_package: verified by the empty lockfile and manifest diff against origin/main
s21d1_062_decision.no_speculative_abstraction: no FGW seam, adapter, interface or configuration key was added in anticipation of the decision

gate_contribution.condition_19: met: the FGW go/no-go decision is recorded as an accepted ADR with the residual evidence it rests on, and the decision adds no dependency

not_in_scope_here: widening the shortlist, which is a D2 change to a pre-registered bound and would invalidate the D1 benchmark if made now
